title: Duplicate & lifecycle
content:
# Duplicate & lifecycle

Validate a Meta create before it spends, pause and resume delivery, duplicate a campaign, ad set or ad, and delete a campaign.

import { Tab, Tabs } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';

Change the state of a hierarchy that already exists: start and stop delivery, copy a level, delete, and validate a create before it costs anything.

## Before you start

Every call here works on a campaign, ad set or ad you already have. You need its platform id from an earlier create or from [`GET /v1/ads/tree`](/platforms/meta-ads/create-ads#reading-the-campaign-tree).

## Pause or resume

`PUT /v1/ads/campaigns/{campaignId}/status` switches one campaign's own on/off switch and nothing else. Its ad sets and ads keep their own switches, exactly as in Ads Manager.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: paused } = await zernio.adcampaigns.updateAdCampaignStatus({
  path: { campaignId: '120250000000000000' },
  body: { status: 'paused', platform: 'facebook' }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
paused = client.ad_campaigns.update_ad_campaign_status(
    campaign_id="120250000000000000",
    status="paused",
    platform="facebook",
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X PUT "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/campaigns/120250000000000000/status" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "status": "paused", "platform": "facebook" }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{ "status": "paused", "platformCampaignStatus": "PAUSED", "statusReadAt": "2026-09-29T08:55:34.565Z", "updated": 1, "skipped": 0 }
```

Pausing a campaign stops delivery for everything under it. Meta reports the children as `CAMPAIGN_PAUSED`.

Resuming it lets each ad set and ad deliver again only if its own switch is on. An ad set or ad you paused in its own right stays paused.

Resume it with `PUT /v1/ads/ad-sets/{adSetId}/status` or `PUT /v1/ads/{adId}/status`, the narrower scopes with the same body. The same rule holds on every ad platform.

Zernio reads the campaign's switch from Meta first:

- If it is already in the requested state, nothing is written and the response says `updated: 0, skipped: 1` with a reason.
- Otherwise the response says `updated: 1`.

`platformCampaignStatus` is the switch read back after the write. `status` is the delivery status that follows from it.

`POST /v1/ads/campaigns/bulk-status` takes up to 50 campaigns and reports each row on its own, so one bad row does not fail the batch.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: bulk } = await zernio.adcampaigns.bulkUpdateAdCampaignStatus({
  body: {
    status: 'paused',
    campaigns: [
      { platformCampaignId: '120250000000000000', platform: 'facebook' },
      { platformCampaignId: '120250000000000002', platform: 'facebook' }
    ]
  }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
bulk = client.ad_campaigns.bulk_update_ad_campaign_status(
    status="paused",
    campaigns=[
        {"platformCampaignId": "120250000000000000", "platform": "facebook"},
        {"platformCampaignId": "120250000000000002", "platform": "facebook"},
    ],
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/campaigns/bulk-status" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "status": "paused",
    "campaigns": [
      { "platformCampaignId": "120250000000000000", "platform": "facebook" },
      { "platformCampaignId": "120250000000000002", "platform": "facebook" }
    ]
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "status": "paused",
  "totals": { "updated": 1, "skipped": 0, "failed": 1 },
  "results": [
    { "platformCampaignId": "120250000000000000", "platform": "facebook", "updated": 1, "skipped": 0, "platformCampaignStatus": "PAUSED" },
    { "platformCampaignId": "120250000000000002", "platform": "facebook", "error": "Campaign not found" }
  ]
}
```

## Duplicate a campaign

`POST /v1/ads/campaigns/{campaignId}/duplicate` copies the campaign, then each of its ad sets, then each of their ads, one Meta `/copies` call per object. Deleted and archived ad sets and ads are skipped.

Meta refuses a single deep copy of 3 or more objects, so copying level by level works for a campaign of any size.

It defaults to `deepCopy: true` with `statusOption: "PAUSED"`, applied at every level. The copy arrives with the full hierarchy and delivers nothing until you activate it.

If any ad set or ad fails to copy, Zernio deletes the partial copy and returns Meta's error, so a retry starts clean.

Each copied object takes Meta a few seconds, so a large campaign takes minutes to answer.

Zernio starts an ads discovery sync after it answers, so the new hierarchy shows up in the tree usually within a few minutes. Pass `syncAfter: false` to skip the sync.

Until the sync finishes, calls that take a copied id answer `404`, so retry them.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: copy } = await zernio.adcampaigns.duplicateAdCampaign({
  path: { campaignId: '120250000000000000' },
  body: {
    platform: 'facebook',
    deepCopy: true,
    statusOption: 'PAUSED',
    renameStrategy: 'DEEP_RENAME',
    renameSuffix: ' (copy)'
  }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
copy = client.ad_campaigns.duplicate_ad_campaign(
    campaign_id="120250000000000000",
    platform="facebook",
    deep_copy=True,
    status_option="PAUSED",
    rename_strategy="DEEP_RENAME",
    rename_suffix=" (copy)",
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/campaigns/120250000000000000/duplicate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "platform": "facebook",
    "deepCopy": true,
    "statusOption": "PAUSED",
    "renameStrategy": "DEEP_RENAME",
    "renameSuffix": " (copy)"
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "copiedCampaignId": "120250000000000013",
  "adSetIdMap": { "120250000000000001": "120250000000000014" },
  "adIdMap": { "120250000000000002": "120250000000000015", "120250000000000003": "120250000000000016" },
  "discovery": "triggered"
}
```

`statusOption` also takes:

- `ACTIVE`, which launches the copy at once
- `INHERITED_FROM_SOURCE`, which mirrors each entity's source status

`adSetIdMap` and `adIdMap` map each source id to its copy.

`renameStrategy` is `DEEP_RENAME`, `ONLY_TOP_LEVEL_RENAME` or `NO_RENAME`, with `renamePrefix` and `renameSuffix`. `ONLY_TOP_LEVEL_RENAME` renames the campaign only.

`startTime` and `endTime` reschedule the copy.

## Duplicate an ad set or an ad

Same shape, one and two levels down. Both create the copy paused by default and accept `syncAfter: false`. An ad set copy with `deepCopy` copies the ad set, then each of its ads, and returns `adIdMap`.

`POST /v1/ads/ad-sets/{adSetId}/duplicate` takes:

- an optional `campaignId` to retarget the copy into another campaign
- `deepCopy` (default `true`, so ads and creatives come along)
- `statusOption`, `startTime`, `endTime` and the rename options

`POST /v1/ads/{adId}/duplicate` takes an optional `adSetId` to retarget the copy into another ad set. It accepts the Zernio ad id or the Meta ad id.

The ad duplicate takes no `platform`, because the ad resolves it.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: adSetCopy } = await zernio.adcampaigns.duplicateAdSet({
  path: { adSetId: '120250000000000001' },
  body: { platform: 'facebook', campaignId: '120250000000000013', statusOption: 'PAUSED' }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
ad_set_copy = client.ad_campaigns.duplicate_ad_set(
    ad_set_id="120250000000000001",
    platform="facebook",
    campaign_id="120250000000000013",
    status_option="PAUSED",
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/ad-sets/120250000000000001/duplicate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "platform": "facebook", "campaignId": "120250000000000013", "statusOption": "PAUSED" }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{ "copiedAdSetId": "120250000000000014", "discovery": "triggered", "raw": {} }
```

Re-running one creative under a different ad set is the ad-level copy:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/66d4a1b2c3e4f5a6b7c8d9e2/duplicate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "adSetId": "120250000000000014" }'
```

Response (`200`):

```json
{ "copiedAdId": "120260000000000003", "discovery": "triggered", "raw": {} }
```

When the native copy requires a creative rebuild, the creative settings Meta returns are preserved. That includes explicit [promotion metadata](/platforms/meta-ads/creatives#promotion-offers) and `creativeFeatures`.

Metadata Meta does not return on the copy cannot be recovered.

<Callout type="warn">
Meta caps a synchronous copy at fewer than 3 total objects, so even a one-ad ad set can trip it. The count appears to include children deleted by earlier copies.
</Callout>

Duplicate the campaign for anything bigger; Meta's own `400` surfaces verbatim.

**Deprecated enhancements.** A creative still carrying Meta's deprecated `standard_enhancements` field blocks the campaign and ad set copies. [Swap the creative](/platforms/meta-ads/creatives#swap-the-creative-on-a-live-ad) first: any edit rebuilds it without that field.

The ad copy drops the field and retries on its own.

## Delete a campaign

`DELETE /v1/ads/campaigns/{campaignId}` cascades on Meta's side, removing the ad sets and ads. It marks the local ad documents `cancelled` in the same pass.

`platform` is required in the body.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: deleted } = await zernio.adcampaigns.deleteAdCampaign({
  path: { campaignId: '120250000000000013' },
  body: { platform: 'facebook' }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
deleted = client.ad_campaigns.delete_ad_campaign(
    campaign_id="120250000000000013",
    platform="facebook",
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/campaigns/120250000000000013" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "platform": "facebook" }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{ "deleted": true, "adCount": 3 }
```

**Empty campaigns.** A campaign with zero ads has no local ad documents to resolve, so this route would `404` on it.

Send `accountId` in the body to delete such a shell. Zernio then skips the local lookup and forwards the delete to Meta. It is ignored when the campaign does have ads.

`DELETE /v1/ads/{adId}` removes one ad and leaves its ad set and campaign in place.

To retire an ad without losing its history, pause it instead. Deleted objects stop reporting.

## Dry-run a create

`validateOnly: true` on `POST /v1/ads/create` runs every node through Meta's own `execution_options: validate_only`.

Nothing is created on Meta and nothing is persisted in Zernio. You get `200` with per-node results instead of an ad.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
import Zernio from '@zernio/node';

const zernio = new Zernio();

const { data: check } = await zernio.adcampaigns.createStandaloneAd({
  body: {
    accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d',
    adAccountId: 'act_1234567890',
    name: 'Spring sale (dry run)',
    goal: 'conversions',
    budgetAmount: 50,
    budgetType: 'daily',
    headline: 'Spring sale',
    body: '20% off everything',
    callToAction: 'SHOP_NOW',
    linkUrl: 'https://example.com',
    imageUrl: 'https://cdn.example.com/banner.jpg',
    promotedObject: { pixelId: '1729525464415281', customEventType: 'PURCHASE' },
    validateOnly: true
  }
});

for (const result of check.results) console.log(result.node, result.status);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from zernio import Zernio

client = Zernio()

check = client.ad_campaigns.create_standalone_ad(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    ad_account_id="act_1234567890",
    name="Spring sale (dry run)",
    goal="conversions",
    budget_amount=50,
    budget_type="daily",
    headline="Spring sale",
    body="20% off everything",
    call_to_action="SHOP_NOW",
    link_url="https://example.com",
    image_url="https://cdn.example.com/banner.jpg",
    promoted_object={"pixelId": "1729525464415281", "customEventType": "PURCHASE"},
    validate_only=True,
)

for result in check["results"]:
    print(result["node"], result["status"])
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/create" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    "adAccountId": "act_1234567890",
    "name": "Spring sale (dry run)",
    "goal": "conversions",
    "budgetAmount": 50,
    "budgetType": "daily",
    "headline": "Spring sale",
    "body": "20% off everything",
    "callToAction": "SHOP_NOW",
    "linkUrl": "https://example.com",
    "imageUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/banner.jpg",
    "promotedObject": { "pixelId": "1729525464415281", "customEventType": "PURCHASE" },
    "validateOnly": true
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "validateOnly": true,
  "results": [
    { "node": "campaign", "status": "validated" },
    { "node": "adSet", "status": "skipped" },
    { "node": "creative", "status": "validated" },
    { "node": "ad", "status": "skipped" }
  ]
}
```

A Meta validation failure comes back as its own `400`, verbatim.

That is the point of the call. Meta's validator catches configuration errors a schema cannot, such as:

- a budget sharing conflict
- a CBO campaign whose ad sets share an optimization goal
- a landing page Meta refuses

Each node reports `validated` or `skipped`, and a skipped one carries a `reason`.

Meta can validate a child only against a real parent. On a fresh tree, the campaign and the creative are validated and the ad set is skipped.

Pass `existingCampaignId` to validate the ad set against that campaign too. The ad is never validatable before create.

<Callout type="warn">
`validateOnly` works on the single standalone shape only. Combining it with `creatives[]`, an `adSetId` attach or `buyingType: "RESERVED"` returns a `400`.
</Callout>

A non-Meta platform returns a `501` with `code: "feature_not_available"`.

**Media uploads.** Media referenced by `imageUrl` is uploaded to the ad account's image library during the dry run, because Meta needs a real image hash to validate the creative.

Uploads are content-deduped, so repeated dry runs add nothing.

## If it fails
A `400` on a dry run is Zernio's own shape check, before the request reaches Meta:

```json
{
  "error": "validateOnly does not support creatives[] yet; it supports the single standalone shape.",
  "type": "invalid_request_error",
  "code": "invalid_field_value",
  "param": "validateOnly"
}
```

Send the single standalone shape for a dry run.

A `404` on the delete means the campaign has no local ads. Send `accountId` in the body to solve it.
